summary: Eastern US Lookouts places a tower near Maxie in the De Soto National Forest; a 1972 newspaper report describes a fatal fall. Current status unknown.

events.note: A man died after falling from the forest fire watch tower near Maxie, per a May 1972 newspaper report quoted on the Eastern US Lookouts page; he is not named here

evidence.supports: 1972 fall from a forest fire watch tower
evidence.quote: fell to his death from a forest fire watch tower over the weekend
on the tower near the Maxie community
Maxie is an unincorporated area in Forrest County, Mississippi

evidence.supports: within the De Soto National Forest; railroad stop
evidence.quote: It lies within the De Soto National Forest and was a stop on the Gulf and Ship Island Railroad
It had a post office from 1900 until 1967.

evidence.supports: 2019: church and cemetery only features bearing the name
evidence.quote: In 2019, a church and cemetery were the only features bearing the Maxie name.

notes_for_editor: No source found gives the build date, height, design or current status. Two web searches returned only directory listings (anyplaceamerica.com, which refused access, and a chamber-of-commerce listing) that are not reliable. A trail-guide page on the Airey Lake towers says four 1930s towers still stand, but names only Airey, so Maxie is not confirmed as standing. The 1972 death is described without naming the man. Record coordinates 30.9543, -89.1886 come from the Eastern US Lookouts page and were not checked against a second source.
